_about: Day 13's golden set. Known questions with known sources, so retrieval and citation
Every question is grounded in text that actually exists in the corpus — the expected
answer fragments were copied from the chunks, not written from memory.
SEEDED STUBS ARE EXCLUDED ON PURPOSE. quarterly_financial_report.pdf,
maintenance_log_Q2.md, FastAPI_Proxy_Architecture.md and test.md contain nothing but
'Placeholder content for a <filename>'. Day 6 measured two of them matching each other
at 0.857 while sharing no subject, and two of the four anchors that set min_score were
stubs scoring on filename echo. A golden set built on them would measure the corpus
UNANSWERABLE cases are not filler. They are what makes insufficient_context
measurable: a system that answers everything scores perfectly on answerable questions

questions.question: What is the formula for the number of blocks in a file?
What is the cost of a binary search on a sorted file?
Where do the live flight positions come from?
Which dataset is used for engine degradation?
How many numbered parts does the project setup document contain in total?
questions._note: Counting is synthesis. The local model answered 4; Gemini answered 5.

WHAT IS THE ADMISSION POLICY
questions._note: Day 18b's regression case, in the user's own wording and capitalisation. The chunk describing the admission process ranked 7th at 0.588 — under the 0.60 floor and outside a top_k of 5 — so the model was handed a refunds table and two page headers and declined. Reported as 'Gemini is broken'. The phrasing matters and must not be tidied: 'Tell me about admission policy' scores the same chunk 0.639 and always worked, which is why this looked intermittent.
